verses.text: It’s actually been reported that there’s sexual immorality among you—the kind even Gentiles don’t accept: a man is sleeping with his father’s wife.
And you’re acting proud instead of grieving, so the man who did this could be removed from your community.
I’m not physically with you, but I’m with you in spirit. I’ve already judged the man who did this, as if I were right there.
When you gather in the name of our Lord Jesus, and I’m with you in spirit, with our Lord’s power present,
hand this man over to Satan so his flesh is destroyed and his spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord Jesus.
Your bragging is out of line. Don’t you know a little yeast works its way through the whole batch?
Clear out the old yeast so you can be a fresh batch, as you already are—unleavened. Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
So let’s celebrate, not with old yeast or the yeast of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in my letter not to keep company with sexually immoral people.
I didn’t mean the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy, swindlers, and idolaters. Then you’d have to leave the world entirely.
What I meant is: don’t associate with anyone who claims to be a believer but is sexually immoral, greedy, an idolater, a slanderer, a drunk, or a swindler. Don’t even share a meal with that person.
Why would I be the one judging people outside the church? Isn’t it your job to judge those inside?
God will judge the people outside. Scripture says, “Remove the wicked person from among you.”
